traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Droseraceae: leaves usually alternate, rarely whorled; leaves usually simple, rarely compound; stipules present or absent; leaf rosettes usually none, often basal; plants hermaphrodite; ovary superior; floral cup present or absent; stems herbaceous; flowers solitary or in cymes; flowers actinomorphic; perianth sepals and petals; fruit capsule; parts of each whorl 4 to 5; stamens (4-) 5 to 20; carpels 3 (-5). Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.vernation.note: Flora of North America vol. 6 (2015), Droseraceae family account (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): blade infolded or circinate in vernation; FOC juvenile leaf blade circinate.

traits.flowering_position.note: Flora of North America vol. 6 (2015), Droseraceae family account (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): inflorescences terminal umbel-like cymes in Dionaea (one species) but lateral circinate or scorpioid cymes in Drosera (nearly all species); FOC flowers axillary, lateral or terminal.

traits.perennation.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Droseraceae: how its perennial herbs last from year to year (character 25), coded often a rhizome, often tubers. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 25 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.inflorescence.note: Flora of China vol. 8 (2001), Droseraceae family account (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowers usually borne in a cincinnus (a coiled one-sided cyme), rarely in a raceme or solitary. Agrees with the family file; raceme added.

traits.rosette.note: Flora of North America vol. 6 (2015), Droseraceae family account (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves in basal rosettes (alternate-cauline in Drosera intermedia); FOC leaves basal and rosulate, or alternate, rarely whorled. Both floras put the rosette first.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Flora of China vol. 8 (2001), Droseraceae family account (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves basal and rosulate, or alternate, rarely whorled (Aldrovanda). Agrees with the family file.

traits.hypanthium.note: Flora of North America vol. 6 (2015), Droseraceae family account (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): perianth and androecium hypogynous; FOC stamens hypogynous.

traits.carpels.note: Flora of North America vol. 6 (2015), Droseraceae family account (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): pistil 3-5-carpellate; FOC 2-5-carpellate; Drosera 3-carpellate (FNA).

traits.stamens.note: Flora of North America vol. 6 (2015), Droseraceae family account (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stamens usually 5 (Drosera) or (10-)15(-20) (Dionaea); FOC 4 or 5. Agrees with the family file.

traits.flower_merosity.note: Flora of China vol. 8 (2001), Droseraceae family account (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): 4- or 5-merous; sepals 4 or 5 (or 6-8). FNA sepals 5, petals 5.

traits.life_span.note: Flora of North America vol. 6 (2015), Droseraceae family account (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): herbs, annual or perennial; FOC perennial or annual. Perennial first: the North American species are mostly perennial.

traits.woodiness.note: Flora of North America vol. 6 (2015), Droseraceae family account (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): herbs.

traits.glandular_hairs.note: Flora of North America vol. 6 (2015), Droseraceae family account (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): blades bearing mucilage-tipped, irritable, multicelled hairs (Drosera) or a hinged trap (Dionaea); FOC sticky glandular hairs or sensitive hairs.

traits.perianth_fused.note: Flora of North America vol. 6 (2015), Droseraceae family account (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): petals 5, distinct.

rules.appearance.organs.leaf.hairs.gland.note: DELTA, Droseraceae (read 2026-10-19), and Flora of North America vol. 6, Drosera: leaves covered with stalked glandular hairs (tentacles) secreting sticky mucilage, often red. That the stalk and head share one colour is the model's.

rules.appearance.organs.basal.hairs.glan.note: As for the stem leaves: a sundew's rosette leaves carry the same red tentacles (FNA vol. 6, Drosera).

rules.appearance.organs.leaf.hairs_benea.note: Flora of North America vol. 6, Drosera (read 2026-10-19): leaf blades with stalked glands on the adaxial surface and margin; the abaxial surface glabrous.

rules.appearance.organs.basal.hairs_bene.note: As for the stem leaves (FNA vol. 6, Drosera): glands on the upper surface and margin only.

appearance.organs.leaf.hairs.glands.colo.why: A sundew's hairs are its tentacles: each a stalk with a sticky gland on top, both in the hairs' stated colour, red in most sundews, not the pale resin of other glandular hairs.

appearance.organs.basal.hairs.glands.col.why: A sundew's rosette leaves bear the same tentacles, in the hairs' stated colour.

appearance.organs.leaf.hairs_beneath.gla.why: A sundew's tentacles stand on the blade's upper face and rim only; its underside is bare.

appearance.organs.basal.hairs_beneath.gl.why: A sundew's rosette leaves bear tentacles on the upper face and rim only.
